findings.topic: Actual sampler, failure and PG path
findings.result: Existing RunSampler(0.1), RetainingSpanProcessor, beginRequestTrace, pg instrumentation and Safe exporters remain unchanged. Explicit mode executes exactly 20 existing ordinary GET /failure requests with two real SELECT ready queries then real SELECT 1/0; no success benchmark or warmup runs in that mode. Root finish uses 500/ERROR, safe CodedError + PostgreSQL cause. Local witness requires exactly 20 distinct roots, actual per-root critical=false, effective sample rate 1, retention error_or_slow, three SELECT spans and one PG error, matching native root ERROR log, and an initially unsampled root. This is a synthetic dev probe, not a production coding run.

findings.topic: Raw delivery accounting inside safe wrappers
findings.result: SafeExporter/SafeLogExporter sanitize first, then observer tees sanitized data to memory and raw OTLP. Raw exporter callback success/failure/throw/pending and flush/shutdown failures are counted independently of Safe wrapper SUCCESS. First callback only is authoritative. No raw transport exception is retained or written. Counts describe exporter invocation batches and records, not HTTP wire attempts or stored backend rows. Receipt success requires all attempted batches/records successful with no failed/pending/flush/shutdown outcomes.

Receipt always has backendObserved=false and actual generated trace/span IDs. Exported-awaiting-backend-verification means local structure and raw callback checks passed; root must subsequently look up those IDs in PostHog. No actual local PG or OTLP send was performed during this review or the author offline tests.

Actual product sanitizer and safeErrorAttributes/causeFields exclude raw error messages, bodies and SQL. SQLSTATE 22012 can survive only in bounded safe cause metadata; private division-by-zero error text must not. Receipt contains source/environment, timings, counts, closed checks/status and actual generated native IDs only. Bad source/configuration goes through closed CLI failure receipt without raw stack/token/DB URL.

Finally closes HTTP connections/listener, ends only owned pool, unregisters pg instrumentation, shuts down both providers, disables global OTel registrations. Provider trace flush precedes log flush. Observer inner shutdown/flush failures remain explicit even where product Safe wrappers suppress exceptions; local checks, incomplete callbacks or cleanup produce exit 1. Bounded PG/client/exporter/workflow timeouts retained. No retry loop added.

Without explicit flag, external OTLP exporters are not constructed. Existing memory-only 100 warm-up pairs, configured default 600 measured pairs, same SQL/retention checks and 20 local failures remain. New control flow isolates export path. Historical overhead remains bound to historical source until the current exact-source default benchmark actually runs.

Old preflight/execute select only acceptance; export selects only existing export; controlled-failure selects isolated new PG17 job. New job has contents:read/id-token:write, no issue-write. Pinned checkout uses exact SHA with credentials disabled. Frozen-lock dependency install and offline guards precede existing OIDC, which selects only prod:/vercel NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY with imports disabled. Always artifact upload includes only safe receipt. Parent independently checked official pinned Infisical action.yaml secret-name support and default nonrecursive behavior; reviewer did not independently access credentials or the external action source.
